entries.en: Only the Commanding Officer may specify a destination for the Normandy.
Congratulations, Commander. Looks like we had a smooth run. You heading down to see the captain?
Sorry, Commander. Just having a chat with Adams down in engineering. Didn't mean to cause any trouble.
With all due respect, sir, maybe he'll finally tell you what we're really doing out here.
If all we're supposed to do is test out the stealth system, why is Captain Anderson in charge? And then there's Nihlus.
Good luck, Commander.
Something I can do for you, Commander?
You and me both. Like I said before, too many things don't add up on this mission.
I don't like turians in general. Runs in my family. My grandfather fought in the First Contact War; lost a lot of friends when the turians hit us.
No, I guess not. But it still makes me nervous to have a Spectre on board, especially a turian.
Understood, Commander.
Yes, sir.
Yes, ma'am.
Sounds like you don't trust our turian guest.
I'm on my way to give him a status update right now.
You think the Alliance brass is holding out on us?
I'll see if I can get some answers when I see him.
I was curious about a few things.
You don't trust Nihlus.
That was thirty years ago. You can't blame Nihlus for that.
Do you have a problem with the captain?
What do you know about the stealth systems?
Info's on a need-to-know basis, Pressly. Just follow the orders you're given.
I better head down and see the captain.
Carry on, Pressly.
I heard you arguing.
He wants to see me.
What do you mean?
I'll look into it.
I have questions.
Goodbye.
Turian Spectre
Captain
Stealth systems
Just do your job.
Goodbye.
That was long ago.
We're an Alliance vessel, human military. But Nihlus doesn't answer to the captain like the rest of us. Spectres operate outside the normal chain of command.
And they don't come along just to observe shakedown runs. Nihlus looks like he's expecting some heavy action. I don't like it.
I just know it masks our location from scans and sensors. Cutting edge technology.
The Normandy's the only ship with this prototype drive. But why are we fully staffed? A skeleton crew would be cheaper. Less chance of security leaks, too.
Plus, there's Nihlus. It's pretty obvious this shakedown run is just a cover.
Damned if I know, Commander. We're out here on false pretenses. I'm not a fan of being left in the dark.
Maybe you're right, Commander. But I just can't shake the feeling that we're out here on false pretenses.
Captain Anderson is one of the most decorated Special Forces officers in the service. If he melted down all his medals, he could make a life-size statue of himself.
You don't send a soldier like that on a do-nothing mission. He's treating this shakedown run too seriously. Something big is going on.
I signed up with the Alliance as a navigator right out of school. Following in my grandfather's footsteps, I guess. My first posting was on the Agincourt.
We were one of the first reinforcements to arrive at Elysium after the Blitz hit. Those raiders were no match for an Alliance frigate.
We were at Elysium during the Skyllian Blitz. A massive fleet of alien raiders hit the colony, trying to wipe it out.
For what?
A full crew makes sense. We need the extra hands in case anything goes wrong. And the Spectre is just here as an observer.
How'd you end up on the Normandy?
A cover?
You're wrong.
Now you're here?
Commander. The turian's waiting for you and the captain in the comm room.
But you have to admit, something's odd about this mission. The whole crew feels it.
No, ma'am! But I can't figure out what he's doing here.
No, sir! But I can't figure out what he's doing here.
I overheard you before. Sounds like you don't trust our turian guest.
You were arguing earlier.
I'm glad you're okay, Commander. Losing Jenkins was hard enough on the crew.
With all due respect, ma'am, maybe he'll finally tell you what we're really doing out here.
Spectres are elite operatives. Top covert agents. Why send a Spectre--a turian Spectre--on a shakedown run? It doesn't add up.
You've got that right, Commander.
Nihlus is no ordinary turian.
Plus, he's a Spectre.
If anyone has to take over for Captain Anderson, I'm glad it's you. Not sure about having non-humans on our ship, though.
With all due respect, ma'am, that's what they said about Nihlus. Look how that turned out.
With all due respect, sir, that's what they said about Nihlus. Look how that turned out.
Yes, ma'am. Understood, ma'am.
Yes, sir! Understood, sir.
Yes, Commander?
I trust you, Commander. If you think they belong here, then so do I.
It's not that, Commander. Humanity has always handled its own problems. Saren attacked one of our colonies. We should be the ones to stop him. We don't need their help.
I guess so. Maybe I'm just stuck in the old ways of thinking. Don't worry, Commander. This won't be a problem.
Of course, the only reason the colony was still standing was because of you, Commander. I can't believe you held out as long as you did.
They had the numbers, but their ships were no match for an Alliance frigate. It was a slaughter. We couldn't even keep track of how many ships they lost.
I got my officer's commission after Elysium. Must have made an impression on the right people. Captain asked for me when he was picking his crew.
We're all on the same team here, Pressly.
I'm in charge here, Pressly. I decide if we have non-humans on this vessel.
Speak freely, Pressly. I want to know if you have a problem with non-humans.
Some people think asking for help is a sign of weakness. That's just being stupid and stubborn. No matter how strong you are, allies can make you stronger.
This is bigger than humanity. Saren's a threat to every species in the galaxy. And I'll welcome anyone who wants to help me bring him down.
How did you end up assigned to the Normandy?
They're on our side.
You doubt my decisions?
Aliens on the ship
Personal questions
Never turn away help.
It's not just our problem.
I can't believe we stole the Normandy!
I know we'll all be court-martialed if this doesn't work out. But part of me loves this!
Congratulations, Commander.
I forwarded the mission update to the Citadel, Commander. We've got confirmation on those reinforcements.
Ambassador Udina wants us to report back to the Citadel. The Council is massing a joint-species fleet to deal with Saren and his geth.
Yes, sir!
Took them long enough. Back to the Citadel, Joker. I want the Normandy at the head of that fleet!
Back to the Citadel, Joker. I want the Normandy at the head of that fleet!
About time!
Let's go.
Yes, ma'am!
I knew they'd come around. Back to the Citadel, Joker. I want the Normandy at the head of that fleet!
Good.
Commander. Something you need?
All right. See ya.
I have to go.
Goodbye.
Message coming in. Patching it through.
You need to turn back, Commander. You're going beyond the range of the operational area.
You went right off the scanners, Commander. Now we have to bring you back.
I prefer gold to silver. You know, for my medal. I figured you'd recommend me for one since I pulled your, uh, boots out of the fire.
Ah, figures. Just get me a nice card and a cake. No coconut, though. I hate that crap.
That's a good point. They'd probably make me shave, too. I spent the last seven weeks working on this baby. No medal's worth that.
Oh, I get it. It's supposed to be a surprise. Don't worry. When they pin it on my chest, I'll pretend I had no idea it was coming.
So, Commander, why don't you tell me why you're really here?
Boy am I glad to be off Noveria. I don't know which was worse: the cold or the corporations.
One will freeze your balls off, the other will sell 'em out from under you. With all due respect, Commander.
Ah, hey, Commander. Next time we touch down, let's try not to park the ship in a colony of mutant zombies. Just thinking out loud here.
Commander. I know it couldn't have been easy for you down there.
Making the call between Alenko and Williams must have been... I'm sorry, sir. I don't know if I could have done it.
Making the call between Alenko and Williams must have been... I-- I'm sorry, ma'am. I just don't know if I could have done it.
I'm not blaming you, Commander. I'm just... it's hard, you know.
Don't worry; I won't let you down. I want to be there when you make that son of a bitch pay!
Aw, damn it. No sign of pursuit? I was hoping the Council would send some ships after us.
I was looking forward to putting the Normandy through its paces. Figured I'd get to see what this ship can really do.
You know, it doesn't seem like much fun when you say it, Commander. So, you need something?
I bet you are the life of the party, Commander. So, you need something?
Sure, Commander. Fire away.
I'll be okay, Commander. I just need some time.
It's a lot shorter than saying Alliance Flight Lieutenant Jeff Moreau. Plus, I love to make little children laugh.
Look, I didn't pick the name. One of the instructors in flight school used to bug me about never smiling. She started calling me Joker, and it stuck.
Hey, I worked my ass off in flight school, Commander. The world's not going to hand you anything if you go around grinning like an idiot.
By the end of the year, I was the best pilot in the Academy. Even better than the instructors. And everybody knew it.
They'd all gotten their asses kicked by the sickly kid with the creaky little legs. One guess who was smiling at graduation.
Of course you do. It's an extremely rare condition. Nobody knows exactly what causes it. Genetic, maybe. It's treatable, but there's no cure.
I can see where this is going. You did a background check on me, didn't you? Well, I'll tell you the same thing I told the captain.
You want me as your pilot. I'm not good. I'm not even great. I'm the best damn helmsman in the Alliance fleet!
Top of my class in flight school? I earned that. All those commendations in my file? I earned every single one. Those weren't given to me as charity for my disease.
You mean-- You mean you didn't know? Ah, crap.
Infect the crew? Ah, man. You have no idea what I'm talking about, do you?
Okay... I've got Vrolik's Syndrome. Brittle bone disease. The bones in my legs never developed properly. They're basically hollow. Too much force and they'll shatter.
Even with crutches and my leg braces it's hard to get around. One wrong step and CRACK! It's very dramatic! But I've learned to manage my condition, Commander.
Put the Normandy in my hands and I'll make her dance for you. Just don't ask me to get up and dance, unless, you know, you like the sound of snapping shin bones.
Saving my "boots" from burning lava is part of your job, Joker. We don't give medals to soldiers for doing their jobs.
If we present you with a medal, you'll end up sitting on stage listening to politicians make speeches for a couple hours.
I want to talk about something else.
There is no right choice for something like that. I just hope I never have to go through it again.
Sometimes making the tough choice is the only way a mission can succeed.
There was no other choice. The mission is more important than one soldier.
Saren's still out there, Joker. Hold it together. We need you.
Saren's still out there. Maybe we'll get a chance to play hide-and-seek with Sovereign.
We're not playing tag, Joker. If they catch us, Saren wins. And we're all dead.
I want to ask you some questions.
Why does everyone call you Joker?
You're dodging the question.
I was just thinking how much you remind me of Santa Claus.
Why didn't you ever smile?
I need to know more about this Vrolik's Syndrome if I'm putting my ship in your hands.
I like to know my crew. Mind if I ask you a few questions?
I'm sorry, Joker. I didn't even know you were sick.
What are you talking about? Are you sick?
I can't have you on this ship if you're going to infect my crew!
How'd you end up joining the Alliance?
How's the Normandy performing? Is she everything they said she'd be?
Earning medals is hard.
You sure you want that?
That's not why I'm here.
Pray you never have to.
That's why I'm in charge.
I had to do it.
We have to move on.
The mission's not over yet.
This isn't a game.
Let's talk.
How'd you get your nickname?
Tell me about your disease.
I just want to talk.
Personal history
Ship Status Report
That's no answer.
Yeah, right.
Were you unhappy?
I didn't mean to insult you.
What disease?
Are you contagious?
They classify my case as moderate to severe. I was born with over a dozen fractures - hips, thighs, ankles. My bones were already breaking in the womb.
A hundred years ago, I wouldn't have survived past my first year. Lucky for me, modern medical science has turned me into a productive member of society.
Whatever you want, Commander.
Uh, I don't fly with my feet, Commander. So I'm fine as long as I'm in this chair. I gotta be real careful when I get up to take a piss, though.
I can do my job as well as anyone else on the ship. Better, actually. So don't worry about it.
The balance isn't what you'd expect. Takes a while to get used to that oversized drive core we got stuffed in the back. Her power can sneak up on you if you're not careful.
I'm not trying to make you uncomfortable. Let's talk about something else.
You're not going to break a bone trying to fly the ship, are you?
Let's change topics.
How do you do your job?
Let's change topics.
If you're looking for an inspirational tale of the crippled kid overcoming impossible odds, you're going to be disappointed.
My mother was a civilian contractor working for the Alliance. I basically grew up on the Arcturus station, back when they were building up the fleets.
Spend all that time around Alliance ships and there's a good chance you'll end up going to the Academy.
She's the best ship in the fleet... if you've got a pilot who knows how to handle her.
The Normandy's probably too much ship for your average Alliance pilot, Commander. Lucky for you, I'm anything but average.
Are you all right?
You're heading off the scanners, Commander.
Commander. Ms. Al-Jilani's story on you just aired.
I don't blame you for blowing her off. She should have made a request through channels.
I'm on your side, Commander. Remember that. This comes from the Joint Military Command.
About what you'd expect. Don't worry too much about it, Commander. They're always angry with us.
Just wanted to let you know what the response was back home.
I won't keep you any longer. Fifth Fleet out.
I have PR people doing spin control. A little memetic engineering, people will forget about this in a week.
I don't blame you for walking out on her.
The brass isn't happy with the way you treated her. This comes straight from the Joint Military Command.
You're probably right. I guess it could have gone a lot worse.
There were better ways to handle it than knocking her on her ass.
As satisfying as that was to see.
Agreed. Most people would be tempted to punch her. But you did the right thing -- you walked away.
Commander, if she'd done that at a bar, she'd go home in an ambulance. But they want me to make this clear. We can't mistreat the press.
She shouldn't have ambushed you like that. But you handled her pretty well.
I don't agree with everything you said. But at least you got her on your side. I just hope it doesn't damage relations with the Council.
Convenient for you, but our allies may not think the same.
When you wear that uniform, you represent the Systems Alliance Military. As a Spectre, you represent humanity.
That would have been true a few weeks ago. Now you're above most humans in their regard.
She shouldn't have ambushed you like that. But you handled it the right way.
You shouldn't have to.
But you were smart enough not to say that. You've got a knack for handling the press.
She was. But we can't say that. There's an art to dealing with the media.
You handled yourself pretty well, Commander. She came across like a raving idiot.
This won't happen again, Commander. We have a press corps so personnel don't have to deal with her kind of B.S.
You don't come off very well. She talked rings around you.
There is one other matter, however.
The Citadel has been trying to play down Saren going rogue. It makes the Spectres look bad.
Your mention of him was politically inconvenient.
I'd appreciate that, Commander.
I wasn't aware of that. I won't discuss him again, sir.
I'm sure Saren "inconvenienced" the people he killed on Eden Prime, too.
How angry was the Council?
Sir, she was going to make me look bad no matter what I said.
I don't have the patience to deal with tabloid gadflies who think they're great journalists.
She wasn't going to let the facts get in the way of the story she wanted to write.
We had differences of opinion, sir. I hope she at least believed my sincerity.
I just told her what she wanted to hear, sir.
The Council can kiss my ass. I'm entitled to my opinions.
I'm not important enough for them to get hysterical over.
I've never had to deal with the press before.
To be honest, I thought she was full of crap.
She wasn't the most sympathetic audience.
I was talking to a wall.
She was distorting my words.
Screw her.
Give me a break.
I did the best I could.
She didn't listen, though.
I fed her a line.
Screw them.
They'll get over it.
I hope so.
Unlike her.
She wasn't listening.
Sorry.
Like I care.
What happened?
That wouldn't have solved the problem. I'm sure it would have felt good, though.
She shouldn't have ambushed you. We have a press corps for a reason. Nobody's blaming you.
With all due respect, Admiral, I'm a soldier. Not a public speaker.
I should've shot her, and dumped the body into a star.
I couldn't just walk away.
I'm no politician.
I should have killed her.
What could I do?
Good timing, Commander. We've got a transmission coming in from the Citadel. Top priority clearance.
Not his signature. I think it's from the Council. I'll patch it through to the comm room.
Commander Shepard. We've received information that may be critical to your mission against Saren.
The Council agreed that Saren was dangerous, Commander. That was why we made you a Spectre. We only balked at unleashing the full force of the Citadel fleet against him.
Nobody on the Council wants to see you fail. So we contacted you with this latest information.
We've received an urgent message from one of our infiltration regiments in the Traverse.
Spectres tend to attract attention, Commander. But they are only one arm of the Council. Special Task Groups are often a better option for monitoring developing situations.
We currently have several infiltration units scattered throughout the border regions of Citadel space. This particular unit was gathering intel on Saren.
We can't have you racing around the galaxy chasing false leads, Commander. We only contacted you because we feel this may be significant.
Unfortunately, the message we received was little more than static. The infiltration team must be in a situation where they can't set up proper interstellar communications.
But the message was sent on a channel reserved for mission-critical communications. Whatever they were trying to tell us, we know it was important.
Considering your interest in Saren, we thought you might want to investigate this. Find out what happened to our team. The signal originated from the planet Virmire.
That unit may have sacrificed their lives to get this message out! Saren is up to something on Virmire. You'd see that if it weren't for your stubborn human pride!
The Council prefers not to become involved in the specifics of Spectre activities. We only want you to be aware of all your options, including Virmire.
Good luck, Commander Shepard. We will keep you advised if we learn anything else.
Is it the ambassador?
I'll take it in the comm room.
What kind of information?
You didn't seem that interested in helping me before. Why now?
You mean spies.
I'm listening.
I don't like being kept in the dark.
What did they find?
A missing infiltration team's not my problem. Clean up your own mess.
Forgive me, Councilor. I'll look into it.
I will find Saren, but I'm doing it my way!
I'll look into it.
From who?
Patch it through.
Tell me.
Now you're helping me?
Infiltration units?
Go ahead.
Why wasn't I told?
And?
I don't have time for this.
Understood.
I'm sorry.
You made your point.
This is my investigation!
I'll take all the help I can get.
Good.
Sounds serious.
Thanks for the info.
Normandy, this is Alliance Command. We're detecting your presence in the Attican Beta Cluster.
One of our surveillance drones was gathering intel on geth activities in the region when it was spotted and shot down.
You need to go groundside and recover the drone's data module before the geth find it.
Commander, urgent message from Alliance Command coming in. I'll patch it through.
Shepard, this is Admiral Hackett from Alliance Command.
We've got a situation here, and you're the only one who can handle it.
You're a Spectre, Shepard. And this isn't some run-of-the-mill mission.
There's an Alliance training ground where we test weapons and technology in live-fire simulations.
One of the VIs we use to simulate enemy tactics in the drills is no longer responding to our override commands. It's gone rogue.
What do you need, Admiral?
How come every time there's a problem, you end up running to me?
How many casualties so far?
Just tell me how to stop it, Admiral.
Synthetic intelligence is a dangerous technology, Admiral.
How can I help?
What's wrong?
I've heard that before.
Was anyone hurt?
What do I have to do?
You should've known better.
We're not stupid, Shepard. This is a virtual intelligence, not a true AI. It's not self-aware, and it can't access any external systems. We didn't do anything illegal here.
Virtual intelligence support is critical to our military success. VIs process thousands of status reports and react in nanoseconds. No human can do that.
Seventeen marines were killed in the simulation exercises before we realized what had happened. That's when we contacted you.
VI support is critical to our military success. They process thousands of status reports and react in nanoseconds. No human can do that.
But as advanced as this thing is at military strategy, it's still just a VI. It's not self-aware, and it's completely disengaged from any networks. That's where you come in.
We need you to fight your way through the training ground to the VI core, and manually disable it.
Our failsafes aren't responding. The VI operates on a closed network. It can't affect any external systems, but we don't have any direct access to its processes.
We could bomb it from orbit, but the damage to the facility would be catastrophic. We'd prefer to have someone shut down the core. Someone like you.
I know Spectres answer to the Council, but you're still human. You're still part of the Alliance military, and right now we need you.
The VI controls all of the facility's weapons, drones, and automated defenses. You're the only one who can pull this off, Shepard. Good luck.
Are you telling me this computer is thinking on its own?
Can't you disable it remotely?
Don't worry, Admiral. I'll take that thing out.
It's gone rogue?
Is that the only option?
I'm on it.
Commander, we've got an incoming distress signal. Patching through to you.
Mayday mayday mayday. This is Lieutenant Marie Durand, 3-14th Infantry, Alliance 10th Frontier Division.
The listening post has been overrun by unidentified hostile life forms. Request immediate extraction.
Commander Shepard, my name is Nassana Dantius. I have a job for you. I can't say any more in an unsecured communication.
If you're interested in hearing my offer, meet me on the Citadel so we can talk in person. I'll be waiting in the diplomat's lounge on the Presidium.
Commander Shepard, I am Nassana Dantius.
I am glad you are here. I must talk to you about my sister, Dahlia. She has been kidnapped by slavers!
I see you got my message.
I do. My sister Dahlia is a crewman on a cargo vessel operating out beyond the fringes of the Traverse. Her ship was attacked by privateers. There were no reported survivors.
This is where it gets complicated. Last week, I received a message with her voice on it. Dahlia is alive!
The rest of the crew was killed, but she was taken prisoner. The slavers demanded a huge ransom from me in exchange for returning her unharmed.
My sister probably told them who she was. My family is very wealthy, Shepard. They must have realized she was worth more to them alive.
That's what I thought. I did what they wanted, transferred the funds to the account they specified. Only, they never released her. They haven't contacted me since.
I've already transferred the funds to the account they specified. Only, they never released her. They haven't contacted me since.
It's too late. I transferred the funds to the account they specified. Only, they never released her. They haven't contacted me since.
I've made a terrible mistake, Shepard. I am a diplomatic emissary! By law, I am required to report any attempted extortion to C-Sec immediately.
But I was afraid for Dahlia, so I just paid the ransom. Now she is still missing, and if anyone finds out what I did I could end up in jail!
Government representatives on the Citadel are not allowed to negotiate with terrorists. It is too dangerous. Paying a ransom would only encourage more kidnappings.
I support the law in theory, but when I got the message, all I could think about was Dahlia's safety.
I doubt they would actually send me to prison for what I did. But they would strip me of my post, and Dahlia would still be in the hands of the slavers.
You only need to bring her back. I have already found her for you.
This is easy money for you, Shepard. I have already found her; you just need to bring her back.
Yes, Shepard? Did you find my sister?
I know you. You're Commander Shepard. The human Spectre.
Dahlia's dead, Nassana. And I know she was blackmailing you.
I killed Dahlia myself. And I know she was blackmailing you.
It sounded like you needed some help.
You said you had a job offer.
I'm sorry for your loss.
You want me to hunt down the people who killed her.
Why didn't the raiders kill Dahlia along with everyone else?
Coming up with the ransom seems like the best way to ensure Dahlia's safety.
Do you want me to deliver the ransom?
You can't negotiate with criminals.
Why would they put you in jail? You're the victim here!
You want me to find her and bring her back.
You got in over your head and you expect me to pull you out?
Dahlia's dead. And I know she was blackmailing you.
Dahlia's dead. I killed her myself. If you don't want to end up like her, start talking!
I know the truth.
Don't lie to me.
Actually, she's dead.
Are you in trouble?
Get to the point.
What do you want?
That's too bad.
Now you want revenge.
I know what this is about.
Why was your sister spared?
You'd better pay.
What's my part?
Don't pay the ransom!
That's a stupid law!
You need my help.
So you came to me.
So I have to fix your mess?
So you came to me.
I found her.
You lied to me!
Hm. And I was all set to try to manipulate you into hunting her down for me. But I guess that won't be necessary now, will it?
I tracked the ransom payment through several accounts. Eventually, it lead to a small mercenary band operating out of the Artemis Tau cluster.
I need you to go to the merc base, take them out, and bring my sister back. You shall be well rewarded.
Thank you, Shepard. I knew you were the right man for the job.
Thank you, Shepard. I knew you were the right woman for the job.
Come back and see me when the job is done.
You are the only one I can turn to, Shepard! Besides, I have already transmitted the coordinates to your ship.
Please, just see what you can do. I will be waiting here when you're done.
So the truth comes out. I hope you are not angry. Surely you can understand why I lied to you?
No need to raise your voice, Commander. Surely you can understand why I lied to you?
If people found out my sister was a criminal, I'd be considered a security risk. They'd revoke my clearance, or place me on administrative leave until she was apprehended.
That is why I misled you. I could not risk you exposing me. But now that Dahlia is out of the picture, it is no longer a problem.
Perhaps you are right. I am sorry. We have trust issues in my family.
I am sorry I wasn't honest with you. We have trust issues in my family.
I could not agree more. She was my sister, but I will not shed any tears for her death.
I shall transfer a little something into your account as a token of my appreciation. I'm sure you will find the amount satisfactory.
You make a good point. Anyone can come up with credits. But I can give you authorization to purchase prototype asari mods.
True, but I am the only one who can authorize you to purchase prototype asari mods.
I will get you added to our manufacturer's preferred client list. I think you would be very interested in what they have available.
Goodbye, Shepard. It has been a pleasure doing business with you.
I do not like being in anyone's debt. Consider it a fee for doing your civic duty if it makes you feel any better.
Or give it away to some charity. I care not. The funds are already on their way. They are your problem now.
Understood, Shepard. I will not bother you again.
I am not that stupid. You will get a fair deal. A very fair deal.
Goodbye, Shepard.
I do not want to take chances with my sister's life. I need a Spectre.
Besides, you operate outside official channels. My superiors cannot find out I never reported the ransom in the first place.
I have resources. Contacts and credits can go a long way, especially if you are willing to bend the rules.
I already broke the law when I paid the ransom. This couldn't make things any worse.
Pretty much what you'd expect: rough, dangerous, and well-armed. Nothing a Spectre cannot handle, though.
Come back and see me when the job is done.
Is there something I can do for you?
What? Are you saying she's...
I gave you what you wanted, Shepard. We have nothing more to discuss.
Thank you for all your help, Shepard.
I don't have time to talk now. I'm very busy.
Keep your reward. I'll bring your sister back. I promise.
